;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**The [[Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights|UNHCHR]] [[Michelle Bachelet]] says she is "horrified" by the deliberate targeting of civilians in the recent [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–present)|offensive]] in northwestern [[Syria]] and accuses the parties involved. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/syria-cites-deliberate-attacks-civilians-200218111516852.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Arts and culture
*An empty [[sarcophagus]] is discovered by archeologists while excavating the [[Roman Forum]]. It appears to be dedicated to [[Romulus]], the founder of [[Rome]]. [https://www.foxnews.com/science/ancient-rome-stunner-sarcophagus-dedicated-to-romulus-discovered (Fox News)]

;Business and economy
*The [[Boy Scouts of America]] file for [[Chapter 11, Title 11, United States Code|Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection]] as the result of multiple [[Boy Scouts of America sex abuse cases|sex abuse lawsuits]]. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/boy-scouts-seek-chapter-11-protection-from-sex-abuse-lawsuits-11582003432 (''The Wall Street Journal'')] [https://www.scoutingnewsroom.org/press-releases/the-boy-scouts-of-america-files-for-chapter-11-bankruptcy-to-equitably-compensate-victims-while-ensuring-scouting-continues-across-the-country/ (Scouting Newsroom)]
*American retailer [[Macy's]] announces it will close 125 stores over the next three years, citing competition from online sellers, including [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2020/02/05/macys-store-closings-list-125-stores-close-19-states/4665130002/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[International sanctions during the Venezuelan crisis]]
**The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] adds [[Russia]]n oil company [[Rosneft|Rosneft Trading S.A.]] to its financial blacklist for helping facilitate the sale of [[Venezuela]]n oil. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/wireStory/us-sanctions-russian-oil-company-role-venezuela-69048227 (ABC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A fire at a library in [[Porterville, California]] leaves one firefighter dead and another missing. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/massive-blaze-california-library-leaves-1-firefighter-dead-1-missing-n1138446 (NBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Chinese state media]] reports that the director of the central [[Wuhan]] Wuchang Hospital has died from the virus. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health/head-of-hospital-dies-in-coronavirus-epicenter-global-economic-impact-spreads-idUSKBN20C03X (Reuters)]
**Russia says it will temporarily block Chinese citizens beginning on February 20 from entering its territory as authorities look to stem the spread of the pandemic. [https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-coronavirus-bans-chinese-citizens-entry/30442161.html (Radio Free Europe)]

;International relations
*[[Russian espionage in the United States]]
**U.S. federal officials charge Hector Alejandro Cabrera Fuentes, a Mexican citizen, in [[Miami]] for allegedly acting on behalf of a Russian agent who recruited him to collect information about the U.S. government and met repeatedly with him in Moscow. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/02/19/us/hector-alejandro-cabrera-fuentes-spying-russia.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.politico.com/news/2020/02/18/mexican-citizen-russia-florida-espionage-115907 (''Politico'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Yukos shareholders v. Russia]]
**A Dutch appeal court reinstates order for [[Russia]] to pay [[United States dollar|$]]50 billion over [[Yukos]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/court-reinstates-order-russia-pay-50-billion-over-yukos-n1137846 (NBC)]
*A court in [[Denmark]] sentences a former public employee to six-and-a-half years in prison for embezzling $17 million in [[Danish government]] funds intended for the poor. She will not appeal the sentence, according to her lawyer. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-denmark-fraud/danish-clerk-gets-six-years-prison-for-stealing-17-million-meant-for-the-poor-idUSKBN20C29Q (Reuters)]
*[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] grants clemency to former [[Governor of Illinois|Illinois governor]] [[Rod Blagojevich]] for [[Rod Blagojevich corruption charges|attempting to sell]] former president [[Barack Obama]]'s [[United States Senate|Senate]] seat in  2008, and pardons former [[New York City Police Commissioner]] [[Bernard Kerik]], [[High-yield debt|junk bond]] salesman [[Michael Milken]], and former [[San Francisco 49ers]] owner [[Edward J. DeBartolo Jr.]] for their numerous felonies and frauds. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/02/18/politics/donald-trump-rod-blagojevich-commutation-sentence/index.html (CNN)]
*A shooting in [[Flint, Michigan]] leaves three people dead. [https://www.abc12.com/content/news/State-police-release-more-details-on-triple-murder-in-Flint-568006791.html (WJRT-TV)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Afghan presidential election]]
**Almost five months after the vote, [[Afghanistan]]'s electoral institution declares incumbent [[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] as the winner of the election. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-election-result/ashraf-ghani-declared-winner-of-afghan-presidential-poll-idUSKBN20C1PZ?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] signs a presidential order sacking senior adviser [[Vladislav Surkov]]. Surkov was in charge of the Kremlin's policy on the [[Ukrainian crisis]] and its relations with the separatist "people's republics" in the [[Donbass]]. [https://www.voanews.com/europe/putin-sacks-top-adviser-and-ex-ukraine-pointman-surkov (Voice of America)]

;Science and technology
*Archeologists announce an articulated [[Neanderthal]] skeleton was unearthed in [[Shanidar Cave]], [[Iraq]], the first discovery of its type in over a decade. They argue the find provided further proof that Neanderthals [[Funeral|buried their dead]], as it was next to a site where similar bodies were found surrounded by [[pollen]] clumps. [https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-51532781 (BBC News)]
